reason: The narrative of Genesis 39 exemplifies the principles of responsible and accountable leadership through Joseph's actions. Joseph is entrusted with oversight of Potiphar's household (וַיַּפְקִדֵהוּ עַל־ בֵּיתוֹ) and later the prison (שַׂר בֵּית־ הַסֹּהַר בְּיַד־ יוֹסֵף), demonstrating clear acceptance of responsibility. His accountability is evident in his refusal to betray his master's trust, stating 'how can I do this great wickedness and sin against God,' showing concern for both his superior's welfare and moral obligation. The repeated blessing upon the households under his management (וַיְבָרֶךְ יְהוָה אֶת־ בֵּית הַמִּצְרִי בִּגְלַל יוֹסֵף) suggests that his responsible stewardship resulted in tangible welfare for those under his charge. The text implicitly models leadership as faithful management of delegated authority with integrity toward both superiors and subordinates.
